The argumentation began with the claim that **AI can make everyday life more enjoyable and convenient**. From there, it argued that **improving everyday convenience supports better health and a higher standard of living**, which then leads to the broader conclusion that **AI is good for society**. Finally, it concluded that **AI should be supported and adopted to benefit society**.

Objections were not actually raised in the provided argumentation record, so there were no specific counterarguments to address or rebut.

**Final answer:**  
Artificial intelligence is good for society. It can make daily life more convenient and enjoyable, help improve health and overall living standards, make work and learning easier for students and professionals, increase accessibility for marginalized groups (especially people with disabilities), and enhance workplace safety.
